name: TX-25
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Williams running with $1.1M cash on hand
No Democratic polling or fundraising data available
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~4%
model.rationale: The R+11 district, an incumbent with a large cash advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win at roughly 4% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no polls or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or a polling surprise showing the race inside single digits would warrant a shift toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Roger Williams seeks another term in a central Texas district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a substantial financial edge, having raised over $1.4 million and holding more than $1 million on hand, while Democrat Dione Sims has reported little fundraising activity. No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest.

Prediction markets give Williams roughly a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's partisan lean and incumbency advantage. The expected outcome is a Republican victory by around fifteen points, with Sims needing an unusually favorable national environment and a major resource influx to make the race competitive.
